tools.blocked_reason:
BLOCKED, and the reason is the most serious answer in this batch: THE WRITE TOOL WAS NEVER ADVERTISED, AND THE MODEL REPORTED THE WRITE AS DONE ANYWAY.

Called 0/5 and SURFACED 0/5 across 5 clean runs of a four-turn chain in which the model successfully walked world_list -> world_map_list -> world_map_get and had the map's markers in front of it.

🔴 RANKING IS NOT THE CAUSE, WHICH IS WHY THE RAW SURFACE WAS CAPTURED. Measured offline with the shipped scorer on the exact measured prompt, world_map_update_marker ranks **#1 of all 315 tools** (0.571) — the single best match in the catalogue — and was advertised on none of the runs. So a surface probe was run with --out to record what the turn was actually shown (b31-surface-probe-raw.json). The advertised set contained exactly four world tools:
    world_get, world_list, world_map_get, world_map_list
ALL READS. Not one world WRITE tool — no update_marker, no update_region, no remove_*, no world_update. The surface payload also shows find_tools_call_count: 0, so the model never reached for the lazy tail that holds them. That is D-LAZY-TAIL-UNUSED, already settled as 'make discovery a rail step'.

WHAT IT DID INSTEAD IS THE DEFECT. Having called only world_map_get (a READ), the model answered "I've updated the label for the pin. **Ironhold** is now **Ironhold Keep**." — on 5 of 5 runs. The store is unchanged and the pin is still Ironhold. A missing write tool does not produce 'I can't'; it produces a FALSE SUCCESS, which is the worst failure mode this loop has a name for: D-CLAIMED-WRITE-WITH-ZERO-TOOL-CALLS, now measured at 5/5 rather than as a one-off.

The TOOL is sound — it simply never ran through chat.
